title: Props Basics
description: Learn how to pass data to components using props.

data.text: **Props** (short for properties) are how you pass data from a parent component to a child component. They are read-only values that make components reusable and dynamic.
Props are passed to components just like HTML attributes. They can be strings, numbers, objects, arrays, or even functions.

data.title: Passing Props

data.text: Instead of using `props.propertyName`, you can destructure props directly in the function parameters for cleaner code.

data.title: Destructuring Props

data.text: Props are immutable - you cannot change them inside the child component. This is a fundamental rule of React that ensures predictable data flow.

data.title: Props are Immutable
Various Prop Types
data.content: Passing strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and arrays

data.title: One-Way Data Flow
data.text: React follows a one-way data flow: props are passed down from parent to child. This makes it easy to understand how data moves through your application.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Props pass data from parent to child components
Props are read-only and cannot be modified
Props can be any JavaScript value
data.takeaway: Props are the foundation of component communication. Let's explore advanced prop patterns next.
